topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, connects the topic to histopathology practicals, and outlines the main learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Discovery of oncogenes through tumor viruses and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the historical study of transmissible tumor viruses, the discovery of captured cellular proto-oncogenes, and the laboratory assays used to test transforming activity.

topics.label: Classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer mutations and examine how allele dosage, the two-hit hypothesis, and dominant-negative mechanisms operate in pathways such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the origins and phenotypic impacts of sequence and chromosomal instability arising from failures in DNA repair, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the step-by-step accumulation of mutations during tumor development and illustrate how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer progression in clinical syndromes.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture, provides recommended reading, and previews the next session on cancer hallmarks.
